The '''creators of SWCCG''' designed Decipher's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game, first released in December 1995. [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]] created its core system. [[Warren Holland]], Decipher's founder, set its direction and approved every card. [[Jerry Darcy]] worked out card details and later led its design.<ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192945/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="bp-sessions">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=1283s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 21:23–23:57. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref>

== How the game was made ==

Braunlich and Tesh, both ''Pente'' world champions, pitched Holland a licensed collectible card game in 1993. It became the [[Star Trek CCG|''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG]] in 1994.<ref name="st-timeline">Kathy McCracken, [http://decipher.com/content/2004/st10/sttimeline.html The History of Star Trek CCG: The Timeline], Decipher (2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080821113824/http://decipher.com/content/2004/st10/sttimeline.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="wp-braunlich">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Braunlich Tom Braunlich], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Braunlich Internet Archive].</ref> Work on ''Star Wars'' began right after that launch, before the license was signed.<ref name="bp-start">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=186s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 3:06–4:40. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref>

The game began as a base each player builds up. The base became the deck, and the deck became the Force a player spends and loses.<ref name="rfd14-force">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=616s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 10:16–12:19. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> Holland's interest in Joseph Campbell's hero's journey led to the split into Light Side and Dark Side.<ref name="bp-campbell">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=535s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 8:55–10:00. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> Through 1995 the team met most evenings in Braunlich's apartment to rework proposed cards, often until 3 or 4 a.m.<ref name="bp-sessions" />

Decipher bought a 70mm print of the films to pull clear frames, and Skywalker Ranch let the team photograph props.<ref name="bp-images">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=1047s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 17:27–19:43. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref><ref name="worlds-special" /> Darcy and [[Bill Martinson]] worked the concepts out in detail, and playtesters such as [[Chuck Kallenbach]] tried to break the game before release.<ref name="rfd14-sw">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=526s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 8:46–10:16. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref><ref name="bp-playtest">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=1831s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 30:31–32:15. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref><ref name="tor-kallenbach">[https://www.theonering.net/torwp/2002/05/17/26593-decipher-talks-lotr-part-1-chuck-kallenbach/ Decipher Talks LOTR Part 1: Chuck Kallenbach], TheOneRing.net (17 May 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195122/https://www.theonering.net/torwp/2002/05/17/26593-decipher-talks-lotr-part-1-chuck-kallenbach/ Internet Archive].</ref>
